title: Optimizing Legal Document Analysis with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ
business: Legal firms managing high volumes of long-form case files and contracts.
problem: Standard models struggle with memory constraints when processing extensive legal documentation, leading to truncation of critical clauses or excessive hardware costs.
solution: Utilizing the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ model allows for efficient 4-bit quantization, significantly reducing memory footprint while maintaining high instruction-following capabilities for complex document analysis.
steps: Install the latest transformers library to ensure compatibility with the Qwen2.5 architecture.
Load the model using AutoModelForCausalLM with device_map set to auto for efficient hardware utilization.
Configure the tokenizer using apply_chat_template to maintain consistent system prompt formatting.
Implement YaRN scaling in the configuration if document inputs exceed 32,768 tokens.
Execute inference using the model.generate method to extract structured insights from legal text.
outcome: Improved throughput and lower memory usage when analyzing lengthy legal documents, enabling faster document review cycles without sacrificing accuracy.
limitation: The use of static YaRN scaling for long-context processing may negatively impact performance on shorter texts; verify by testing model response quality across varying input lengths.

code.content:
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
# Load the quantized model
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ", device_map="auto")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ")
# Prepare input with template
text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
inputs = tokenizer([text], return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
# Generate analysis
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
